notes.title: Development Update: A New Focus
notes.content:
Dear LithoBreak Community,

We hope this message finds you well. We want to take a moment to thank each and every one of you for your continued support and enthusiasm for LithoBreak. Your feedback and engagement have been invaluable to us as we work to make this game the best it can be.


Pause on Episode Development

We have an important update to share regarding the development of Episode 1 and future episodes.

After careful consideration, we’ve decided to temporarily offload work on the episodes during early access. This means that while we have updated the Steam 'default' branch to include multiplayer functionality, it does not include Episode 1 content.

We understand that this news may be disappointing, knowing most of you have enjoyed Episode 1 and are eagerly awaiting Episode 2. However, we believe this decision will ultimately benefit the game and the community in the long run. By focusing on completing and polishing the core gameplay loop, we can ensure a more robust and engaging experience for everyone in all game modes.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/ae7bbc6e9fe673de50d2c736ad79501e17f9827a.png


Why This Change?
[olist]
 Improved Story Content: When we reintroduce the story content, it will be refreshed and be built atop a solid foundation of core gameplay mechanics. This allows us more creative freedom and ensures a seamless experience.
 Resource Efficiency: Maintaining Episode 1 through development is resource-intensive for our small team. Offloading this work allows us to focus our efforts on enhancing the core gameplay and adding new features.
 Access to Original Episode 1: For those who wish to experience the original Episode 1, we’ve added an 'ogepisode1' branch on Steam. This way, you can still enjoy the story content while we work on bringing you an even better experience in the future.
[/olist]
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/ef023a5ba99380cc4526d64ea3e30b7942327d40.png


Current Development Focus

Here’s an update on where we are at and what we’re working on:

 Multiplayer Testing: We’ve recently completed a round of testing, open to everyone who had purchased LithoBreak, to validate that multiplayer functionality works seamlessly. Thank you to everyone who participated in this testing phase!
 First-Person Mechanics: In direct response to the feedback received through the multiplayer testing, we’re adding more first-person mechanics to give multiplayer gameplay more depth and meaning. This includes animated character models and Gadgets (holdable and useable items) that players can utilize.
 Community Poll for Next Gadget: We’re excited to involve you in the development process! We are hosting a week-long community poll to decide what the next Gadget should be over on Discord.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/d90968af1501440d627d471c9bccc6af8c34fa58.png


Looking Ahead

While this shift in focus may be challenging in the short term, we are confident that it will lead to a more polished and enjoyable game for all. We appreciate your understanding and patience as we make these necessary adjustments. Your feedback and support are crucial to us, and we encourage you to share your thoughts and ideas.

Following the Gadgets mechanics will come the much anticipated Custom Buildings and Custom Vehicles, so stay tuned for that!

Thank you for being a part of the LithoBreak journey. Together, we can create something truly special.

Warm regards,

The LithoBreak Development Team

notes.title: May Video Update
notes.content:
Greetings LithoBreak Community!
We're back with our May monthly video update, bringing you the latest on our game development progress. This month's highlights include:

Standardizing Parts:
We've started reshaping our parts to standardize them across equipment, reducing the number of unique parts and aligning them with hexagon grids. This makes parts more versatile and gameplay more streamlined.

Grid System Expansion:
We've expanded our grid system, introducing nested grids of different sizes - 1m, 3m, and 9m. This new system will simplify gameplay from personal item placement to configuring larger equipment.

Material Transfer Mechanism:
We've developed a material transfer mechanism that allows efficient material movement between equipment pieces, utilizing our new hexagonal grid system. Watch the video to see how it works in action.

State Machines for Equipment:
We're transitioning our equipment systems over to state machines, making them easier to maintain and improving game performance.

[previewyoutube=x2xthzfEhJY;full][/previewyoutube]

We continue to appreciate your support and feedback. We invite you to join our community discussions here on Steam and on our social media channels (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn).

Happy building, and see you on the moons!

The LithoBreak Team

notes.title: July Dev Log - Closed Beta Changes
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/3f5986b6a8c968bbd06a9f05ce1f084408fa8299.png

Greetings, scientists! 

It’s been a bit since our last dev log because we wanted to keep the surprise, but now the Closed Beta is live, and we can share what LithoBreak’s development has been over the last few weeks!


https://i.imgur.com/MjDNJbD.gif
New UI Style
Our UI has seen massive improvements for the release of the Closed Beta, with the new UI style translated to the tablet! 
The UI overhaul we started a few weeks ago for the game is now nearing completion, the most recent upgrade being the tablet. Those UI changes mean migrating the game to thinner and sleeker borders, which are nicely complemented by brand new smooth and quick fade transitions between tablet tabs!


https://i.imgur.com/mFrPjoq.gif
Autosave and Save/Load Improvements
After listening to our Discord community’s feedback, we took the time to improve our saving and loading system, and we’re glad to announce it has been radiation-hardened and is now ready for service!

We pushed a lot of standardization efforts in our game development, meaning loading games between versions will be far more reliable. Allowing you to keep growing your mining operations after most game updates without starting over.

Additionally, we implemented a new autosave feature! It will save your game automatically between intervals. Players can customize the interval time and the number of saved files in the game settings.

Settings, you say?


https://i.imgur.com/IUrpUJ9.gif
Settings Menu
That’s correct; we have been working hard at adding a fully-fledged settings screen to LithoBreak! 

You can find this new Options menu on both the title screen and the in-game tablet, so you can switch settings on the fly if the need arises. This new menu will allow the game to run on a wider variety of devices and should cover most of the screen available to players!
You can also take advantage of the Options menu to rebind your keyboards to something that suits your style better.

Let us know if you’d like to see this added to the mining screen! We are always listening to incoming feedback on our Discord.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/f919f733cc778ec392c0eb1613a87e41fcc3abae.png
Deconstruction & Parts Durability 
The latest feature we added to LithoBreak has been a highly requested one: Deconstructing buildings! You can now tear apart buildings you no longer want to make room for another production line or make your base more efficient or aesthetically appealing. 

Also, every building will now have a list of all the installed parts, anywhere between 20 and 80 parts per building. As the buildings are used, the HP percentages of the components will slowly drop, and some will need to be replaced! Better materials will lead to higher durability while building parts, and high durability parts will degrade a lot slower. More to come in the next Dev Logs.


https://i.imgur.com/Ho5zDuZ.gif
Polish to the Moon!
After many hours of hard work, we're glad to say that LithoBreak is looking better than ever! Everything has been revamped, upgraded, or tweaked from the station to the moon to make the game experience as appealing as possible.

Thanks to our awesome alpha testers, gameplay has been improved and is as smooth as it’s ever been. 

Next up will be some beta testing! Our Closed Beta session is running strong thanks to our incredible community, and we will share the results and improvements from that feedback in the next Dev Log. But before that, we want to give you all an opportunity to join in on the fun!

Until August 3rd, the Beta will be accessible to everyone through Steam! Head up to:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1091030/LithoBreak/

And join the playtest here! Share your feedback with us on Discord and chat with the devs and the rest of the Beta testers.

Thanks for joining us in this Dev Log, and we hope to see you in the next one! In the meantime, don’t miss out on LithoBreak’s development by following our socials:
Twitter: https://twitter.com/LithoBreakGame
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/LithoBreakGame
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/LithoBreakGame/

Catch you in the Verse,
Tau Ceti Labs

notes.title: May Dev Log - Terrain Expansion
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/1e01d82b4ce17ba42739d88482dd4298e8a99e7e.png

Greetings, scientists!

May is over, and with it comes our Dev Log for the month! We’re really excited to share the progress we’ve made this month with you. So grab a seat, a nice cup of coffee, and let’s jump in!


https://i.imgur.com/BODz1ZA.gif

This month we focused heavily on expanding the game’s current features, and polishing it in preparation for the next steps of development. This included expanding the current map’s terrain (we may or may not be looking into procedural terrain options ;) ), releasing tooltips in the mining UI to provide more information, and a major lighting overhaul that required us to completely rework the way the scenes are built into the game. But, let’s jump into those new features shall we?


https://i.imgur.com/6PBCtZ3.gif
Terrain Expansion:
As mentioned, we expanded the terrain greatly, and now the players will have 9 times as much terrain to explore and build on! This includes more variations in the terrain (including mountains and dunes), and more constructible terrain: The hex grid we showed off last month will be generated all the way to the edge of the map. 

To accommodate such an expansion, we adjusted the camera: It now has more zoom levels for you to admire your base and assess your next production lines!


https://i.imgur.com/24O6DP9.gif
Tooltips and Highlights:
A lot of time was spent expanding and refreshing the highlights and tooltips in LithoBreak. The biggest one being, you are finally able to show multiple tooltips on screen simultaneously! This allows you to compare the input/output for multiple buildings and makes it easier to set production lines, or plan your next mining operation. 

From a developer standpoint, we reworked the tooltips to be easier to implement and maintain in the long run, meaning we can expand or change them quickly and efficiently.

To be able to do so however, we will need your feedback! It will be crucial to let us know what needs changed or where more context is needed. You’ll get a chance to help us out in our upcoming Closed Beta! But more information on that later. ;)


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/ae7bbc6e9fe673de50d2c736ad79501e17f9827a.png
Lighting Update:
The lighting for the entire station has been overhauled. This not only improves the game graphically to provide a much more thematic experience depending on which room the player is in, but also provides a huge performance boost. We shifted our internal workflow for using lights, allowing more flexibility in setting lighting sources up, and a more stable framerate while exploring the space station.


https://i.imgur.com/ypotFAz.gif
That’s a wrap for this month everyone! The feature rework and polishing we focused on will allow us to have a much more stable platform for the next steps of our development, meaning a lot more changes coming in the upcoming months. Stay tuned on Discord, and keep your ears open, the upcoming closed beta is rapidly approaching, scientists!

Catch you in the Verse,
Tau Ceti Labs

notes.title: April Dev Log - Episode 1 Rework
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/ca41a0fd9e33085431803cc76079178b82e5e8f3.png

Greetings, scientists!

April has been a crazy month for us, and we are super excited to show you what we have been working on today! We apologize for being a bit late for this Dev Log, but trust us it’s worth it. So as usual, take a seat, grab a coffee, and dive with us on what April was all about for Lithobreak!


https://i.imgur.com/TG3k5l2.gif
Episode 1 Rework:
This month we heavily focused on refreshing and reworking the Episode 1 for LithoBreak, and it is shaping up to be a major overhaul of the entire game! While we had our work cut out for us, we’re proud to say we have made huge steps towards the final version of the Episode. Once we finish getting everything together, we will hold a limited access Closed Beta for you to try it out before anyone else. We are always looking for our community’s feedback to help shape LithoBreak into the best version of itself, so gathering that feedback in our Closed Beta test is extremely valuable to us. 

Throughout the process of completing Episode 1, we improved the gameplay experience by adding in  a new voiceover for our main characters, and a heavy rework of some mining mechanics; some of those changes are detailed below.


https://i.imgur.com/OTuTzmp.gif
New Voiceover:
Part of the Episode 1 rework includes a brand new voiceover, giving Eli and Sara more lines and enhancing the story. While the player expands their material gathering and part production operations, the two characters will engage in more comedic conversations. A lot of those will be dropping tips about the mining flow, and help the player figure out the best materials to make even better parts.

This voice over will provide a deeper dive into Sara’s character, and greatly expand her lore! We won’t spoil it there though. ;)


https://i.imgur.com/68B81t6.gif
Mining Camera:
After hearing feedback from our community on Discord, we decided to rework the camera from scratch. It will now behave like a more classic orbit-style camera. We spent a lot of time smoothing the camera movements out to make sure everything is set correctly, and will give the player nice feedback while moving around their mining operations.

To help with base navigation, we implemented higher zoom levels to watch your base from afar, but it’s still possible to zoom close to the ground and buildings to see the finer details! These new changes will allow the player to play in a more familiar top-down perspective, as is cherished in classical base building games.


https://i.imgur.com/ohsKroO.gif
Hex Grid:
A very big change has been implemented in the last couple weeks that we’re absolutely stoked to introduce today: A hexagon based building grid!

This grid will help you place your buildings in a more detailed way, thus making your mining operations easier! The grid is generated based on the moon’s topology, so the player can instantly know if a spot is viable terrain for a new building or not.

All the current buildings in the game have been modified to fit the grid layout properly, and any new additions will follow this same grid pattern. This will be a very nice feature to test out if you’re lucky enough to get in our planned Closed Beta. ;)

This grid will fit very nicely with our reworked camera mentioned previously. The top down view combinated with the new Hex grid will make planning your base much easier and your operations smoother!

https://i.imgur.com/iHJzznO.gif

That’s it for this month, scientists! Thanks for sticking with us till the end, and we hope you’re as excited as we are for these new features! If you want a sneak peek at what we’re working on next, make sure to join our Discord, and to check out our Dev Live Streams.

Catch you in the Verse,
Tau Ceti Labs

notes.title: March Dev Log - Visual Improvements
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/abe8275bb39f39f46ccfd45b63cc71b49c06b430.png

Greetings, Scientists!

We have been working hard on more features and improvements for our game, and we are very excited to show them off to you today! So pull up your seat, grab a cup of coffee, and join us while we discuss what’s been done behind the scenes of LithoBreak this past month!


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/3c7df71bd5101aa12527f7b9ff7fed40f83c606a.png
Buildings Visual Improvements:
We are spending some time reworking the visuals of various buildings in the game, making them more lively and appealing.  For example:
 The ingots will now glow while cooling off
 Substance fillings will be animated and material levels show in the buildings
 Vacuum rocket engine exhaust! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/f8a4345b7951a58c09080e5d3fb1c7bd6ce58b2e.png
New Main Console UI:
A lot of work was put into reworking the UI, and after a lot of community feedback provided on our Discord, we’re happy to show off the final result! 

The new UI is simpler to operate, and fits the new style of the game better
 The build menu is now on the lower left and easily accessible.
 Sprites and link connections overlay can be turned on and off on the right.
 An (in progress) parts list is available, with more information windows to come.
 The updated objectives will show up on the top left.
 SARA tags along too, showing up on the top of your screen.
 With everything closed the UI has a slick look!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/f79cff4e118bb05cc4ecd77a77fae6935f5cc8f3.png
Part Transport Revamp:
Something we wanted to improve was the part transportation system we’re using in game. We have recently overhauled the core systems to be more performant and flexible

The major impact now is the removal of the noticeable lag spikes and allows part warehouses for storage.  In the near future, we will extend this transportation infrastructure to include multiple locations via train networks and orbital transports!

The solution we have come up with is capable of handling hundreds of part types with thousands of individual parts across dozens of mining sites. If you are interested in the technical aspect, here it is;
 The different part types have separate mappings, allowing calculations to be split up.
 Part routes and production requests are calculated over multiple frames and cached for future access.
 When a part state changes, the remaining routes or requests for that type are ignored and flagged for recalculation.

This approach greatly diminishes the amount of calculations needed, and distributes the calculation load over time for a drastically smoother experience.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/d4465e20f408df18531eab02e7b2b7d38d0ced8a.png


Thanks for taking the time to check out or dev log, Scientists! We’re really excited about the recent changes and what’s coming next, and we hope you’re just as hyped as we are! We’ll talk to you soon, but in the meantime, make sure to check out our Dev Live Streams, and to join us on Discord!

Catch you in the Verse,
Tau Ceti Labs

notes.title: February Dev Log - Episode 1 Rework
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/08d9f8a615f296c45ea5cb1ab8855b1f636ad401.png

Greetings, Scientists!

February ended in the blink of an eye, and before we knew it we were already in March! We hope you’re as excited as we are for all the new stuff we've been working on including various refreshes of mechanics, and the progress we made on the Ceramics Processing!


https://i.imgur.com/MkdnZGT.gif

New Builds and Feedback:
We’re stoked to announce that the main branch for the game has been updated with everything from our January post! We also want to thank you for all the constant feedback you provided in our Discord. We have been working hard on the changes the community suggested so we can make sure it is the best version of itself as we come close to re-releasing Episode 1!

As we are ramping up development of the reworked episode, we are testing out all the new improvements, and incorporating feedback on a weekly basis!


https://i.imgur.com/QiWyljB.gif

Objectives Refresh:
We have been hard at work freshening up the objectives and associated screens for the game, including completely revamping the objectives to be more flexible and responsive to the Player’s situation in game! All those changes will allow us to create more varied objective types in the future as well, giving us plenty of room to expand the game storyline.

You can now also play messages directly from the Objective Screen, making the game progression smoother and avoiding unnecessary navigation in the tablet.

When selecting objectives on screen, the objective now expands downwards to show all the options available. When a selection is made, the screen resizes around the selected option and the unselected ones animate, fitting the game UI nicely!


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/2e725c64c7a1fa4a83696efeecac8671522003c0.png

Ceramics Refresh (WIP):
We have simplified the Sifter, making it work more predictably and less RNG based. The processing speed is determined by a set volume input rate, making it process a starting substance with 50% Silica twice as fast as a starting substance with 25% Silica into purified Silica. 

The Mixer “Recipe” (what the unit will produce) will soon be set directly from the given inputs, meaning:
 Setting Silica to the top slot and Alumina to the middle slot will produce Fire Brick materials
 Setting Alumina to the top slot and Silica to the middle slot will produce Kiln Brick materials

I know it is short and sweet, but we have so much more lined up still to update you on soon! We hope you’re as happy as we are about these changes, and we’ll see you again soon! In the meantime, make sure to check out our Dev Live Streams, and join us on Discord!

Catch you in the Verse,
Tau Ceti Labs

notes.title: January Dev Log - A Fresh Start
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/5b0734253d0b0c78b3d1bbfc25dc69e187e20abe.png

Happy New Year, Scientists!

We’re excited to share our first Dev Log of the year with you all! This month’s update is mainly about metallurgy, resource links, as well as a first-look into our manufacturing room, currently in development. So sit back, grab your coffee, and jump on in!

Metal Buildings Update

https://i.imgur.com/647Hdfk.gif
Multiple buildings are currently in the works and can be seen coming to life on our Twitch channel! If you’re interested in seeing more behind-the-scenes work, make sure to jump in, subscribe and sit in with us while we develop the game!

There are 3 different buildings that can now produce metal ingots: the Inert Smelter, the Reaction Smelter, and the Allow Furnace. Each of these buildings will create different variations of metal ingots that you can use in manufacturing a vast amount of items later down the line. 

Here is a brief rundown of their respective ingot production:

 The Inert Smelter converts Alumina powder into Aluminum, but requires vast amounts of energy to produce ingots.

 The Reaction Smelter will allow you to make iron and chromium ingots through aluminothermic reactions.

 The Alloy Furnace takes specific metals in, and melts them down to create different alloys, like 304L stainless steel which, fun fact, is the same steel grade used on the SpaceX Starship!

Once production is complete, haulers will then move ingots and materials between buildings based upon how you link your resources.

Revamped Resource Links

https://i.imgur.com/mUzQ9Bx.gif
We are always working hard to make the Lithobreak experience even better, and recently have worked hard on some nice QOL changes that we’re sure you will love!

Sources and sink nodes now have smooth transitions between buildings, sprites, and window locations, making for a more fluid gameplay experience. This can be seen most notably when turning on and off the building sprites using the lower right sprite toggle.

Resource links can now also handle ceramic substance and metal ingot routing. The different substance types are color coded for better visibility and easier set up of production lines. In the future, resource links will handle fluid piping routes as well!

Manufacturing Update

https://i.imgur.com/qa7ic7t.jpg
Our artist has been hard at work designing the metal processing buildings, but has also made a lot of progress on the station's next largest room, the Manufacturing Room!

This new room will house many metal printers of different sizes to supply different building parts, which will be extremely helpful to kickstart the moon mining operations on the horizon!

Thanks everyone for reading this month’s Dev Log! See you next month for more, and in the meantime you can check out our Dev Live Streams and join us on Discord!

Catch you in the Verge,
Tau Ceti Labs

notes.title: December Devlog
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/a6d0b28d28cbc1c62bd88dc767d35be0c80342b5.png

Greetings Scientists!

This year has been full of changes in our lives, but also in terms of Lithobreak development. Starting this month, we will be providing our players monthly development updates. We would like to include everyone in this journey and be more transparent with everything moving forward. We also have our Head Developer Moe stream Lithobreak's development twice a week on Twitch, so if you are interested in seeing it live, do join us!

Without further ado, lets jump into our current state and recent development:

New Roadmap
A roadmap for the game has been added to the title screen. We wanted a way to show sneak peeks at what’s to come, and the new UI design that we are working on. Do note that this roadmap does not fully represent all our plans, just the ones that are finalized and scheduled in the full roadmap.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/780d2da2faa744e987a246011ab390953c995ede.jpg

More about the roadmap: We are revealing our plans for “voxelized” moons. Allowing true-to-life sized moons to be explored and exploited for resources. The roadmap will be periodically updated as finalized decisions are made in its development. 

New Agroponics Room
The Agroponics room will be accessible in-game soon. This is one of the largest rooms in the station so far, complete with fruits, vegetables, and mushrooms to be harvested. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/908c138a8b4b0c7489aec60baab50fd8405c9ad4.png

Agroponics room features the following:
 Sized to keep a maximum of 15 fed (Even though there’s only Eli in the station).
 Provides produce for the kitchen robotics to support well-rounded diets (for all walks of life).
 Integrated with the waste processing systems of the station for sustainability.

Episode 1 feature is completed
The updated script for episode 1 is finalized, and new voice clips will be added to ease players into gameplay. Sara has a bit more explaining to do when it comes to messing with the mining console (instead of just cutting Eli mid-sentence).

https://i.imgur.com/elE9knE.gif

Ceramics have been completely revamped since the start of early access. Materials are now a finite set, with materials being routed around with nodes. More game mechanic polish to come, such as simplifying the sifter etc.

Introduction to Metal buildings and QoL Improvements

 Metal buildings are now in development (more information soon).
 Development videos are on Twitch (We stream twice a week!).
 New buildings cover the production and processing of base metals and metal alloys.
 Metals ingots will now be routed around the moon much like ceramics.
 Starting metals are produced in the inert smelter.
 More advanced metals are produced in the reaction smelter, which consumes another metal in the process.
 Alloys are produced in the alloy furnace to attain higher material properties.
 Different properties will be important when it comes to producing parts in various factory types including casting, forming, machining, and moulding.


Thank you so much for reading our Devlog, and making it to the end! More will be coming soon.

Don't forget to join our discord and have a chat with the LithoBreak team! Invite Link: Discord

Also, follow us on our socials for up to date news and announcements! Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram. 

May the Verse be with you,
Tau Ceti Labs

notes.title: Materials Update
notes.content:
The revamped mining experience has just gone live!  This comes with major overhauls to the core mining systems, including:

Materials
Every material is now of a pre-defined list with color codes, making it easier to differentiate between materials.  These changes allow easier development of future materials, and many more materials and material types will be coming soon.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/113f021f1d1d7426420d4aef9ed25d4a2460b74e.png

Material routing
Through the updated UI, materials are now intuitively routed between buildings.  This gives a clearer picture of how the different materials are being moved through a base.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/8bfb1ecc90d42228ec4d4aa6bcecf5cfe2a93525.png

Parts handling
How the parts are handled and saved on the back end have been reworked for performance reasons.  This mainly impacts the builder when there are hundreds of possible part locations to install parts into, as seen in the new title screen!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/02092f9661fd56ef8cec5a26a9929746bed80eab.png

Thank you for your patience as we focused on rebuilding the mining foundation of LithoBreak.  Many more changes will be coming soon to build off this new foundation, including a revamped part production coming to the powder printer.  Later we will be extending the mining experience to include new types of materials like metals and fluids.

We hope you enjoy this update!

notes.title: We heard you like improvements
notes.content:
As we wrap up work on the mining revamp, we have also been taking time to improve the LithoBreak experience across the board.  All of these improvements are now live on the public test branch and will be making it to the main branch in the coming weeks.

Smoother gameplay

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/adc266b128897e751b7d3de0d59e312b4087de65.png

With the major changes to the core mining mechanics, the Episode 1 objectives sequence has been reconfigured accordingly.  We also took the chance to make the sequence more focused on the part production flow.  This new sequence can be previewed in the test branch and early feedback is highly welcome.

Upping our color game

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/3aacf896adac6821311de59e045ab95a231ef7bd.png

An appealing recent change has been migrating our in-game colors to a true color pallet.  This includes making sure specific colors are dedicated to 'player interactable' elements for a more intuitive interface.  The change is already a drastic improvement and we are in the process of implementing the pallet across all of the UI elements in the test branch.

Integrating feedback

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/09b3bb719695e31430f732cebe9c58a26430bb89.png

We continue to implement significant changes and fixes on top of the massive mining revamp that itself was undertook based upon community feedback.  This includes:


 Migrating the in-game guide to the 'tablet' space in the console. (ongoing)
 Station lighting changes.
 Balancing mining experience. (ongoing)
 Menacing satellites correctly enter orbit directly in front of the station.
 Multiple explorations of possible mechanics to be announced later.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38362143/e09ac60ffa6f12fc81a705b84abf70408aae49f4.png

We are excited to be bringing the mining revamp to the main branch soon and start implementing new mining infrastructure upon this improved foundation.  We would love to hear interesting suggestions on what mechanics would be interesting as we implement new mining system into LithoBreak.  Let us know in the forums or on Discord.

- Tau Ceti Labs Team

Stay safe in the verse

notes.title: Playtest with Science
notes.content:
We are excited to announce that we have begun playtesting the first episode of LithoBreak!  This has been years in the making and we know there is much more work to be done.

Access to the playtest can be requested midway down the LithoBreak store page.  There will initially be limited playtest slots, though we aim to include every signup in due time.

When you do get access, please direct feedback to the discussion forum.  We will be keeping our eyes on that space to incorporate feedback and prioritize planned features.  This playtest will include ongoing updates in the form of gameplay polish and updated artwork.

We hope you enjoy the playtest and we look forward to your feedback!

- Team TCL
